skill.name: starknet-js
skill.description: Build Starknet applications with starknet.js v9.x across providers, accounts, contracts, wallets, fees, paymasters, signing, and deployment workflows.
skill.summary: Apply practical starknet.js v9.x patterns for reliable Starknet reads, transactions, account operations, and wallet integrations.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most of the 98 findings are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, documentation terms, and safe placeholders. Confirmed items cover package installation, live credential access, and third-party RPC or paymaster endpoints. No prompt injection, secret exfiltration, command injection, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The connectivity example loads a private key even though it only reads the chain ID and account address.
remediation.suggestion: Use RpcProvider alone for connectivity checks. Put signing in a separate testnet example that uses an isolated wallet or managed signer.

remediation.issue: The quick start instructs users to install a third-party package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed starknet.js version, commit a lockfile, and review package provenance and lifecycle scripts before installation.

remediation.issue: Several examples use fixed third-party RPC and paymaster endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Accept endpoints through configuration, verify the chain ID, document provider trust, and define fallback behavior.

content.value_statement: Starknet integrations require careful handling of providers, accounts, fees, and transaction states. This skill provides focused starknet.js v9.x patterns for those workflows.
actual_capabilities: Configure RpcProvider connections and perform read-only Starknet queries.
Create or connect accounts and prepare signed transaction workflows.
Read and write contracts with typed calls, calldata helpers, and multicalls.
Simulate transactions, estimate fees, set resource bounds, and inspect receipts.
Integrate browser wallets, paymasters, message signing, token operations, and contract deployment.
limitations: Examples target starknet.js v9.x and may require changes for other SDK versions.
The skill does not author Cairo contracts or provide a formal security audit.
Live workflows require trusted RPC services, funded accounts, correct ABIs, and deployed contract addresses.
Transaction examples need application-specific authorization, spending limits, secret storage, and user confirmation.

use_cases.title: Add wallet transactions
use_cases.description: Connect browser wallets, track account changes, submit calls, and report final transaction states.

use_cases.title: Build contract services
use_cases.description: Create provider and account services for contract reads, writes, simulations, fees, events, and receipts.

use_cases.title: Automate sponsored flows
use_cases.description: Plan paymaster transactions, multicalls, fee policies, retries, and operational checks for controlled automation.

prompt_templates.title: Read a contract value
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal starknet.js v9.x TypeScript example that connects to Sepolia and reads a contract value. Explain required inputs and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Submit a safe contract write
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement an account-based contract write with simulation, fee estimation, and receipt checks. Use environment variables for configuration. Never print signing secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate a browser wallet
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a browser wallet flow with explicit account and network change handling. Include transaction confirmation and clear rejection states.

prompt_templates.title: Design a sponsored multicall
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a sponsored multicall using a paymaster. Add policy checks, spending limits, simulation, fallback handling, and monitoring guidance before execution.

output_examples.input: Read an ERC-20 balance on Starknet Sepolia.
output: A provider configuration using a caller-supplied Sepolia RPC URL.
A typed contract read that preserves token values as BigInt.
Validation and error handling for missing addresses or failed RPC requests.

output_examples.input: Prepare an approve and deposit multicall.
output: A two-call transaction plan with compiled calldata.
A simulation step and fee estimate before submission.
Receipt handling that distinguishes success, revert, rejection, and RPC failure.

output_examples.output: A paymaster flow with supported-token checks, sponsorship policy validation, fee estimation, spending limits, and explicit fallback behavior.

best_practices: Verify the chain ID, simulate writes, estimate fees, and confirm final receipts before reporting success.
Keep signing credentials outside source code and prefer wallet, hardware, or managed signer boundaries.
Use BigInt for token values and apply bounded retries only to transient provider failures.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode production private keys, account credentials, or unreviewed transaction payloads.
Do not convert token balances or fees to JavaScript Number values.
Do not submit transactions without authorization checks, fee limits, simulation, and network validation.

faq.question: Which starknet.js version does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It targets starknet.js v9.x. Verify constructor signatures and method behavior against your installed version.

faq.question: Can this skill write Cairo contracts?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on TypeScript SDK integration with deployed Starknet contracts.

faq.question: Does it support browser wallets?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers wallet connection, account changes, network changes, and transaction execution patterns.

faq.question: Does it support sponsored fees?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes paymaster setup, sponsorship mode, alternative gas tokens, and fee estimation guidance.

faq.question: How should private keys be handled?
faq.answer: Use an isolated signer, wallet, hardware device, or managed secret service. Never commit or print a production private key.

faq.question: Is the example ready for production?
faq.answer: No. Add trusted endpoints, authorization policy, spending limits, secure signing, monitoring, retries, and application-specific validation.
